# Exact decimal column sum CLI

## Rationale

A tightly defined command-line contract gives users and automation reproducible decimal totals across valid inputs and predictable rejection of invalid inputs while leaving implementation technology open.

## Problem

Command-line users processing CSV data need a predictable way to select a named column and obtain an exact decimal total; ambiguous decoding, CSV interpretation, decimal syntax, precision, and failure reporting can otherwise produce inconsistent or unusable results.

## Users

- Command-line users who need an exact total for a named CSV column.
- Automation and data pipelines that consume deterministic JSON results and errors.

## Goals

- Provide a deterministic CLI named decimal-column-sum that sums one exactly named CSV column from one document on stdin.
- Preserve exact base-10 decimal value and input scale without bounded-precision rounding or exponent notation.
- Make accepted input, rejected input, output channels, JSON property order, messages, and exit status observable and deterministic.

## Non-goals

- Prescribing an implementation language or library.
- Supporting encodings, CSV dialects, decimal forms, or header-matching rules beyond the stated contract.
- Trimming, normalizing, repairing, or skipping nonconforming headers, records, or selected values.

## Workflows

- A user invokes decimal-column-sum with exactly --column <header>, supplies one CSV document on stdin, and consumes the single JSON result from stdout.
- A user may submit a header-only document and receive a successful zero-row result; each blank logical data record is processed as a real one-field record.
- When invocation, input, or I/O is invalid, automation consumes one JSON error from stderr and the corresponding nonzero exit status, with no stdout or partial sum.

## Success measures

- For every accepted document, the selected values are summed exactly with arbitrary-precision base-10 integer arithmetic at the maximum input fractional scale; with no data rows the scale is 0.
- Successful output is one LF-terminated compact JSON object on stdout, in fixed column,rows,scale,sum property order, with no stderr and exit status 0.
- The rendered sum has exactly the resulting scale and no exponent notation; negative zero is rendered as unsigned zero while retaining that scale.
- Valid strict UTF-8 and the specified CSV forms are interpreted consistently, including one optional leading UTF-8 BOM, quoted embedded line endings, and an optional final record ending.
- Every malformed or out-of-contract invocation, input, or I/O condition produces no stdout and one LF-terminated compact JSON error on stderr in fixed code,message property order, using a fixed locale-independent message and no partial sum.
- Exit status is 2 for USAGE; 3 for INVALID_UTF8, EMPTY_INPUT, MALFORMED_CSV, INVALID_HEADER, COLUMN_NOT_FOUND, ROW_WIDTH_MISMATCH, or INVALID_DECIMAL; and 4 for IO_ERROR.

## Scope

- Read exactly one strict UTF-8, comma-separated CSV document from stdin; accept one leading UTF-8 BOM and reject malformed UTF-8 or NUL.
- Parse double-quoted fields, doubled embedded quotes, LF or CRLF record endings, quoted embedded line endings, and an optional final record ending; reject bare CR, unterminated quotes, and characters after a closing quote before a separator or record end.
- Use the first logical record as the header, require all decoded header fields to be nonempty and unique, and match --column exactly without trimming, case folding, or Unicode normalization.
- Treat zero-byte input as EMPTY_INPUT, a header-only input as a successful zero-row sum, and blank logical data records as real one-field records rather than ignored input.
- Require every data row to match header width and every selected value to match -?(0|[1-9][0-9]*)(\.[0-9]+)? exactly; reject plus signs, exponents, whitespace, disallowed leading zeros, and empty values.

## Constraints

- The invocation requires exactly --column <header>.
- Input is confined to the stated UTF-8 and CSV contract, and invalid input is rejected rather than repaired.
- Header selection uses exact decoded text identity without trimming, case folding, or Unicode normalization.
- Summation uses arbitrary-precision base-10 integer arithmetic at the maximum fractional scale present in selected input values.
- Success and failure outputs use compact JSON, fixed property order, strict stream separation, and one terminating LF.
- Error messages are fixed and locale-independent with this exact code-to-message mapping: USAGE -> "expected exactly --column <header>"; INVALID_UTF8 -> "input is not valid UTF-8"; EMPTY_INPUT -> "input CSV is empty"; MALFORMED_CSV -> "input is not valid CSV"; INVALID_HEADER -> "header fields must be nonempty and unique"; COLUMN_NOT_FOUND -> "requested column was not found"; ROW_WIDTH_MISMATCH -> "data row width does not match header"; INVALID_DECIMAL -> "selected field is not a valid decimal"; IO_ERROR -> "input or output failed". # Exact decimal column sum CLI

## Rationale

A tightly defined command-line contract gives users and automation reproducible decimal totals across valid inputs and predictable rejection of invalid inputs while leaving implementation technology open.

## Problem

Command-line users processing CSV data need a predictable way to select a named column and obtain an exact decimal total; ambiguous decoding, CSV interpretation, decimal syntax, precision, and failure reporting can otherwise produce inconsistent or unusable results.

## Users

- Command-line users who need an exact total for a named CSV column.
- Automation and data pipelines that consume deterministic JSON results and errors.

## Goals

- Provide a deterministic CLI named decimal-column-sum that sums one exactly named CSV column from one document on stdin.
- Preserve exact base-10 decimal value and input scale without bounded-precision rounding or exponent notation.
- Make accepted input, rejected input, output channels, JSON property order, messages, and exit status observable and deterministic.

## Non-goals

- Prescribing an implementation language or library.
- Supporting encodings, CSV dialects, decimal forms, or header-matching rules beyond the stated contract.
- Trimming, normalizing, repairing, or skipping nonconforming headers, records, or selected values.

## Workflows

- A user invokes decimal-column-sum with exactly --column <header>, supplies one CSV document on stdin, and consumes the single JSON result from stdout.
- A user may submit a header-only document and receive a successful zero-row result; each blank logical data record is processed as a real one-field record.
- When invocation, input, or I/O is invalid, automation consumes one JSON error from stderr and the corresponding nonzero exit status, with no stdout or partial sum.

## Success measures

- For every accepted document, the selected values are summed exactly with arbitrary-precision base-10 integer arithmetic at the maximum input fractional scale; with no data rows the scale is 0.
- Successful output is one LF-terminated compact JSON object on stdout, in fixed column,rows,scale,sum property order, with no stderr and exit status 0.
- The rendered sum has exactly the resulting scale and no exponent notation; negative zero is rendered as unsigned zero while retaining that scale.
- Valid strict UTF-8 and the specified CSV forms are interpreted consistently, including one optional leading UTF-8 BOM, quoted embedded line endings, and an optional final record ending.
- Every malformed or out-of-contract invocation, input, or I/O condition produces no stdout and one LF-terminated compact JSON error on stderr in fixed code,message property order, using a fixed locale-independent message and no partial sum.
- Exit status is 2 for USAGE; 3 for INVALID_UTF8, EMPTY_INPUT, MALFORMED_CSV, INVALID_HEADER, COLUMN_NOT_FOUND, ROW_WIDTH_MISMATCH, or INVALID_DECIMAL; and 4 for IO_ERROR.

## Scope

- Read exactly one strict UTF-8, comma-separated CSV document from stdin; accept one leading UTF-8 BOM and reject malformed UTF-8 or NUL.
- Parse double-quoted fields, doubled embedded quotes, LF or CRLF record endings, quoted embedded line endings, and an optional final record ending; reject bare CR, unterminated quotes, and characters after a closing quote before a separator or record end.
- Use the first logical record as the header, require all decoded header fields to be nonempty and unique, and match --column exactly without trimming, case folding, or Unicode normalization.
- Treat zero-byte input as EMPTY_INPUT, a header-only input as a successful zero-row sum, and blank logical data records as real one-field records rather than ignored input.
- Require every data row to match header width and every selected value to match -?(0|[1-9][0-9]*)(\.[0-9]+)? exactly; reject plus signs, exponents, whitespace, disallowed leading zeros, and empty values.

## Constraints

- The invocation requires exactly --column <header>.
- Input is confined to the stated UTF-8 and CSV contract, and invalid input is rejected rather than repaired.
- Header selection uses exact decoded text identity without trimming, case folding, or Unicode normalization.
- Summation uses arbitrary-precision base-10 integer arithmetic at the maximum fractional scale present in selected input values.
- Success and failure outputs use compact JSON, fixed property order, strict stream separation, and one terminating LF.
- Error messages are fixed and locale-independent; their exact code-to-message mapping remains to be supplied by the blocking product question.

## Rationale

## Problem

Command-line users processing CSV data need a predictable way to select a named column and obtain an exact decimal total; ambiguous decoding, CSV interpretation, decimal syntax, precision, and failure reporting can otherwise produce inconsistent or unusable results.

## Users

- Command-line users who need an exact total for a named CSV column.

## Goals

- Provide a deterministic CLI named decimal-column-sum that sums one exactly named CSV column from one document on stdin.
- Preserve exact base-10 decimal value and input scale without bounded-precision rounding or exponent notation.
